full_judgment:
This Rule arising out of an application under section 25 of the Small Cause Court, Act 1887, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 25-6-1997 passed by the learned Judge of the Small Causes Court and Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in SCC Suit No.3 of 1995. 

 The learned Judge of the SCC after considering the evidence on record, decreed the suit with the finding that the admitted tenancy of the defendant under the plaintiff had legally been terminated after service of notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, and since the defendant was found to be a defaulter, he is liable to be evicted. 

 4. Being aggrieved the defendant-tenant preferred this revisional application assailing the judgment on the ground that the learned subordinate Judge, SCC Judge) committed illegality in decreeing the suit. 

 7. Admittedly, the defendant was inducted in the possession of the suit property on the basis of a written agreement as a monthly tenant with a fixed rent payable within 1st five to ten days of each month. The second agreement dated 1-1-1989 is admitted in evidence as Exhibit 2. As per terms of the agreement if monthly rent remains unpaid within the aforesaid stipulated period the tenancy so created is liable to be terminated. It is also evident that there being no renewal of the second contract, the tenancy under the written deed expired on 31-12-1993. It appears from the Annexure A submitted with the counter-affidavit of the opposite party dated 5-3-2000 that the defendant instituted House Rent Case No. 19 of 1984 under section 19(I) of the Premises Rent Control Act and the learned Assistant Judge being Ex-officio Rent Controller, on hearing both the parties, dismissed the case with the finding that the defendant tenant had already made himself a defaulter in paying rent in accordance with section 18(5) of the Rent Control Act, by his judgment and order dated 13-8-1997. Against the said judgment, the defendant-tenant preferred to file Miscellaneous Appeal No. 226 of 1997, which was also dismissed on 4-3-1999. It appears from Annexure A of another Counter-Affidavit dated 23-10-2002 that the plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 14 of 2000 against the defendant-tenant for realisation of accumulated arrear rents for 40 months and the said money suit was decreed with the clear, finding that the defendant was a defaulter in paying rents. The defendant has not been able to show that he paid monthly rent regularly within the stipulated period of the written contract. Thus it appears that the defendant was rightly adjudged as ejectable monthly tenant as per terms of the contract.
